Grad-CAM Localization Significance and Layer Sensitivity — Run 2¶

Why this notebook exists¶

The primary Grad-CAM evaluation notebook found near-zero Dice/IoU and 0/103 Pointing Game hits at model.layer4. Visual inspection of the saved qualitative figures shows something more nuanced than "no signal": the CAM consistently produces a single, spatially coherent, anatomically-plausible hot region, and the small tumor frequently sits at or near its edge -- sometimes inside it (the "Best" example, Dice=0.063), sometimes just outside (the "Worst"/"Median" example). This is not what pure noise looks like, so it needs a properly-designed statistical test rather than a snap judgement in either direction.

This notebook fixes a flawed comparison from the earlier analysis and adds two experiments to resolve the ambiguity:

  1. Corrected per-patient random-location null. The earlier test compared actual peak → that patient's tumor centroid (76.9 voxels) against a random point → the volume's geometric center (77.5 voxels) -- two different reference points, which is not a valid comparison. The correct null is: for each patient, generate many random points and measure their distance to that same patient's own tumor, then compare the actual CAM peak's distance against that patient-specific random distribution.
  2. Minimum distance to the tumor mask, not just centroid distance. Pointing Game (peak literally inside the lesion) is an extremely strict test given tumors can occupy well under 1% of the volume. Distance-to-nearest-tumor-voxel captures "how close was the near-miss," which the qualitative figures suggest matters a lot here.
  3. Layer3 vs. layer4 sensitivity. layer4's feature map is only ~16x10x12 before upsampling; layer3 is shallower and less downsampled, and may retain more spatial precision. Both results are reported honestly regardless of which looks better -- this is a sensitivity check, not a search for the best-looking layer.

This notebook reuses the same model, checkpoint, dataset, and label-audit discipline as the primary Grad-CAM notebook. It does not retrain anything and does not replace the primary notebook's results -- it resolves an ambiguity in how to interpret them.

# ============================================================
# CELL 2 — PATHS AND DATA LOADING
# ============================================================

def resolve_processed_path(raw_path, subfolder_name, processed_dir):
    normalized = str(raw_path).replace("\\", "/")
    prefix = f"{subfolder_name}/"
    while normalized.startswith(prefix):
        normalized = normalized[len(prefix):]
    return processed_dir / f"{subfolder_name}/{subfolder_name}/{normalized}"


def load_volume_and_mask(row, processed_dir, return_raw_mask=False):
    image_path = resolve_processed_path(row["image_path"], "images", processed_dir)
    mask_path = resolve_processed_path(row["mask_path"], "masks", processed_dir)
    volume = np.load(image_path).astype(np.float32)
    raw_mask = np.load(mask_path)
    if volume.shape != raw_mask.shape:
        raise ValueError(f"Shape mismatch for {row['study_id']}: {volume.shape} vs {raw_mask.shape}")
    tumor_mask = (raw_mask == PDAC_TUMOR_LABEL)
    if return_raw_mask:
        return volume, tumor_mask, raw_mask
    return volume, tumor_mask


split_df = pd.read_csv(SPLIT_PATH)
test_df = split_df[split_df["split"].str.lower() == "test"].reset_index(drop=True)
pdac_test_df = test_df[test_df["diagnosis"] == "PDAC"].reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"PDAC test cases: {len(pdac_test_df)}")

sample_path = resolve_processed_path(pdac_test_df.iloc[0]["image_path"], "images", PROCESSED_DIR)

# ============================================================
# CELL 3 — MODEL RECONSTRUCTION
# ============================================================

def build_model():
    model = r3d_18(weights=None)
    old_conv = model.stem[0]
    new_conv = nn.Conv3d(
        in_channels=1, out_channels=old_conv.out_channels,
        kernel_size=old_conv.kernel_size, stride=old_conv.stride,
        padding=old_conv.padding, bias=False,
    )
    model.stem[0] = new_conv
    model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, 1)
    return model


model = build_model()
checkpoint = torch.load(CHECKPOINT_PATH, map_location=DEVICE, weights_only=False)
model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state"], strict=True)
model = model.to(DEVICE)
model.eval()

print(f"✓ Run 2 checkpoint loaded (epoch {checkpoint['epoch']}, "
      f"val_loss={checkpoint['best_val_loss']:.4f}).")

Cell 4 — Grad-CAM class (identical to the fixed version in the primary notebook)¶

In [4]:
# ============================================================
# CELL 4 — GRAD-CAM CLASS
# ============================================================

class GradCAM3D:
    def __init__(self, model, target_layer):
        self.model = model
        self.activations = None
        self.gradients = None
        self._forward_handle = target_layer.register_forward_hook(self._save_activation)
        self._backward_handle = target_layer.register_full_backward_hook(self._save_gradient)

    def _save_activation(self, module, inputs, output):
        self.activations = output.detach()

    def _save_gradient(self, module, grad_input, grad_output):
        self.gradients = grad_output[0].detach()

    def remove_hooks(self):
        if self._forward_handle is not None:
            self._forward_handle.remove(); self._forward_handle = None
        if self._backward_handle is not None:
            self._backward_handle.remove(); self._backward_handle = None

    def _clear_state(self):
        self.activations = None
        self.gradients = None

    def generate(self, volume):
        self.model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        self._clear_state()
        logit = None
        score = None
        try:
            logit = self.model(volume)
            if logit.numel() != 1:
                return None, np.nan, "invalid", {"reason": "unexpected logit shape"}
            score = logit.reshape(())
            if not torch.isfinite(score).item():
                return None, np.nan, "invalid", {"reason": "non-finite logit"}
            probability = float(torch.sigmoid(score).detach().cpu().item())
            score.backward()
            if self.activations is None or self.gradients is None:
                return None, probability, "invalid", {"reason": "hooks did not fire"}
            if not torch.isfinite(self.activations).all().item() or not torch.isfinite(self.gradients).all().item():
                return None, probability, "invalid", {"reason": "non-finite activations/gradients"}
            weights = self.gradients.mean(dim=(2, 3, 4), keepdim=True)
            cam = (weights * self.activations).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
            cam = F.relu(cam)
            target_size = volume.shape[2:]
            cam = F.interpolate(cam, size=target_size, mode="trilinear", align_corners=False)
            cam = cam.squeeze().detach().cpu().numpy()
            if not np.isfinite(cam).all():
                return None, probability, "invalid", {"reason": "non-finite CAM"}
            cam_min, cam_max = float(cam.min()), float(cam.max())
            if cam_max - cam_min < 1e-8:
                return np.zeros_like(cam, dtype=np.float32), probability, "degenerate", {}
            cam_normalized = ((cam - cam_min) / (cam_max - cam_min)).astype(np.float32)
            return cam_normalized, probability, "ok", {}
        finally:
            self._clear_state()
            del logit
            del score

Cell 5 — Experiment 1 + 3: corrected per-patient random null, and minimum-distance-to-tumor¶

For each case: locate the CAM peak, compute its distance to the nearest tumor voxel (via a Euclidean distance transform -- this is Experiment 3, replacing the earlier centroid-only distance), then generate many random points in that same volume and compute the same distance-to-tumor for each of them (Experiment 1's corrected null: same target, same volume, only the query point differs between "actual" and "random"). This gives a fair, per-case comparison rather than mixing two different reference targets.

In [5]:
# ============================================================
# CELL 5 — CORRECTED LOCALIZATION SIGNIFICANCE TEST
# ============================================================

def run_localization_diagnostic(target_layer, target_layer_name, df, processed_dir, model,
                                 n_random=N_RANDOM_BASELINE_PER_CASE, seed=SEED):
    gradcam_local = GradCAM3D(model, target_layer)
    rows = []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    for i, (_, row) in enumerate(df.iterrows()):
        volume, tumor_mask, raw_mask = load_volume_and_mask(row, processed_dir, return_raw_mask=True)
        volume_tensor = torch.from_numpy(volume).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).to(DEVICE)
        cam, probability, cam_status, _ = gradcam_local.generate(volume_tensor)
        if cam_status != "ok":
            continue

        peak_index = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(cam), cam.shape)

        # Distance from every voxel to the nearest tumor voxel (0 inside the tumor).
        # distance_transform_edt(~tumor_mask): tumor voxels are False (background)
        # in the inverted mask, so non-tumor voxels get their distance to the
        # nearest False (i.e. nearest tumor voxel); tumor voxels get 0.
        edt = distance_transform_edt(~tumor_mask)
        actual_dist = float(edt[peak_index])

        # Per-patient random null: same volume, same tumor, only the query
        # point differs -- this is the corrected comparison.
        D, H, W = tumor_mask.shape
        rz = rng.integers(0, D, size=n_random)
        ry = rng.integers(0, H, size=n_random)
        rx = rng.integers(0, W, size=n_random)
        random_distances = edt[rz, ry, rx]
        random_median = float(np.median(random_distances))
        random_mean = float(random_distances.mean())
        pct_random_beaten = float((random_distances > actual_dist).mean())  # >0.5 = better than chance

        rows.append({
            "study_id": row["study_id"], "layer": target_layer_name,
            "probability": probability, "tumor_voxel_count": int(tumor_mask.sum()),
            "actual_dist_to_nearest_tumor_voxel": actual_dist,
            "random_mean_dist": random_mean, "random_median_dist": random_median,
            "normalized_score": actual_dist / max(random_median, 1e-6),  # <1 = closer than random
            "pct_random_beaten": pct_random_beaten,
        })

        if (i + 1) % 20 == 0 or (i + 1) == len(df):
            print(f"    [{target_layer_name}] {i+1}/{len(df)}")

    gradcam_local.remove_hooks()
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Cell 8 — Enhanced qualitative figure: CT + tumor contour + CAM + peak marker + distance annotation¶

Directly connects the quantitative distance metric to what it looks like on the actual volume, for a couple of representative cases (the same "worst" case examined in the primary notebook, plus the case with the best normalized score here).

In [8]:
# ============================================================
# CELL 8 — ENHANCED QUALITATIVE FIGURE WITH DISTANCE ANNOTATION
# ============================================================

def plot_case_with_distance(study_id, df_source, processed_dir, model, target_layer, ax_row, title_prefix):
    row = df_source[df_source["study_id"] == study_id].iloc[0]
    volume, tumor_mask = load_volume_and_mask(row, processed_dir)
    volume_tensor = torch.from_numpy(volume).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).to(DEVICE)

    gradcam_viz = GradCAM3D(model, target_layer)
    cam, probability, cam_status, _ = gradcam_viz.generate(volume_tensor)
    gradcam_viz.remove_hooks()

    peak_index = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(cam), cam.shape)
    edt = distance_transform_edt(~tumor_mask)
    dist_to_tumor = edt[peak_index]

    z = peak_index[0]

    ax_row[0].imshow(volume[z], cmap="gray")
    ax_row[0].contour(tumor_mask[z], colors="lime", linewidths=1.5)
    ax_row[0].set_title(f"{title_prefix}: {study_id}\nCT+tumor, CAM-peak slice z={z}")
    ax_row[0].axis("off")

    ax_row[1].imshow(volume[z], cmap="gray")
    ax_row[1].imshow(cam[z], cmap="jet", alpha=0.5)
    ax_row[1].contour(tumor_mask[z], colors="lime", linewidths=1.5)
    ax_row[1].plot(peak_index[2], peak_index[1], marker="x", color="white", markersize=14, markeredgewidth=3)
    ax_row[1].set_title(f"Grad-CAM + peak marker\ndist to tumor = {dist_to_tumor:.1f} voxels, prob={probability:.3f}")
    ax_row[1].axis("off")

Conclusion¶

This notebook resolves the ambiguity left by the primary Grad-CAM evaluation by replacing an invalid statistical comparison (actual peak-to-tumor distance vs. random-point-to-volume-center distance -- two different reference targets) with a proper per-patient null (actual peak vs. many random points, both measured against that same patient's own tumor location), adding a minimum-distance-to-tumor metric alongside the strict Pointing Game, and checking whether the finding is specific to layer4 or also present at the shallower, higher-resolution layer3.

How to interpret the printed results above:

  • mean_pct_random_beaten near 0.5 at both layers → the earlier near-chance finding holds up under a correct statistical test.
  • mean_pct_random_beaten meaningfully above 0.5 with a small Wilcoxon p-value → there is a real, if coarse, localization signal, consistent with the qualitative pattern seen in the saved figures (one coherent hot region, tumor often at its edge) -- in which case the primary notebook's Dice/IoU/Pointing Game numbers should be reported as evidence of imprecise rather than absent localization, a materially different and more defensible claim.
  • A meaningful difference between layer3 and layer4 → report both honestly as a resolution-dependent finding, rather than treating either as more "correct."

This notebook does not, by itself, tell you which of these turned out to be true -- that depends on the actual printed numbers from your run. Whichever result you get, it should replace the "no better than random" language from the earlier interpretation with whatever this corrected test actually shows.
